entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Apollophanes Soter was an Indo-Greek king who ruled over eastern and central Punjab in modern India and Pakistan from approximately 95 BCE until his death in 60 BCE. He played a crucial role in maintaining the stability of the region, particularly during the tumultuous period known as the Indian Succession Crisis.

Apollophanes' reign was marked by his efforts to promote trade and commerce along the ancient Silk Road, which connected India with Central Asia and the Mediterranean region. His diplomatic relations with neighboring kingdoms, including the Ptolemaic Kingdom in Egypt, helped to secure peace and stability in the region.

Despite facing numerous challenges, Apollophanes' leadership and strategic decisions ensured the continued prosperity of the Indo-Greek kingdom, paving the way for its eventual expansion into new territories. His legacy as a skilled diplomat and military strategist has endured, making him one of the most notable figures in Indian history during the Classical period.

The inscription on the Apollophanes Pillar, discovered in 1898, provides valuable insights into his reign, including his titles and accomplishments. This pillar is now housed at the Archaeological Survey of India in Delhi, serving as a testament to the enduring legacy of this enigmatic king.
